newsitem.title: UK: Redland profits slump, sees better H2.
newsitem.headline: Redland profits slump, sees better H2.

text.p: Redland Plc, the UK building materials group, was the latest in the sector to report a sharp dive in half year pretax profits on Thursday, due to weak markets and bad weather, but it pointed to a pick-up in the second half.

Pretax profits for the six months to June 30 fell to 95 million pounds ($148.6 million) from 165.2 million last year. Turnover dropped to 1.18 billion from 1.29 billion and the dividend was frozen at 5.5 pence per share. Trading in the second half so far has matched 1995 levels and should be ahead for the six month period, due to cost savings, said Redland.

Looking at a breakdown of the figures, the European tiling business RBB saw operating profits of 69 million pounds, down from 119.4 million. The business was hit by adverse winter weather, which delayed building projects across Europe and hit the entire sector. Poor German and French markets also hit trading.
Aggregates saw an operating profit of 27.5 million pounds, down from 35.0 million, with the UK market hit by sluggish market conditions and low spending on roads and other infrastructure.
France saw worsening conditions, leading to plans for 250 employees to be axed this year. Redundancy costs will be levelled by savings. 1997 will see a seven million pounds saving.

But North American aggregates proved to be more resiliant. Asia Pacific operations saw operating profits of 3.2 million pounds versus 2.4 million. Bricks and other businesses saw profits of 3.2 million pounds against 16.2 million, reflecting the sale of the Terca and Monier divisions. ($1=.6392 Pound)
